newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insolvencies growing fastest in Europe.
newsitem.headline: German insolvencies growing fastest in Europe.

text.p: German insolvencies grew at more than 15 percent in 1996, the fastest rate of increase across Europe, business research group Dun & Bradstreet's German subsidiary said on Tuesday.
Overall, corporate insolvencies across 14 countries rose 6.5 percent to 207,000 firms over the year, costing around a trillion marks in unrecovered debts and unemployment-related costs, it said.
In Germany, the 25,800 business failures carried with them a total cost to the economy of around 80 billion marks, Dun & Bradstreet estimated.

France and Britain also recorded high insolvency rates of 64,000 and 41,100 respectively. Dun & Bradstreet said figures in these two countries had to be seen within the context of laws making it easier for creditors to instigate insolvency proceedings.
